headline: DeepSeek, the Chinese AI lab, plans to lead a seed funding round for Winverse AI, a robot-brain start-up founded this year by a former Tencent scientist, Bloomberg reports.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 1: Bloomberg's report is dated 12 Oct 2026, before the window, and the round is a plan not yet completed.
importance_line: Robotics researchers and rival AI labs are watching a major Chinese model maker move from robot bodies, through Unitree, to robot brains, but the round is a plan reported by one outlet, Winverse has shown no product and the deal is not completed.
summary: Bloomberg reported on 12 Oct 2026, as relayed by 36Kr, that DeepSeek plans to lead a seed round of tens of millions of dollars for Winverse AI, a start-up founded this year by Hu Han, a former Tencent distinguished scientist who led its vision-language and embodied-intelligence model teams, at a post-investment valuation of about $400 million. It would be DeepSeek's second robotics bet in two months after its roughly 141 million yuan stake in Unitree Robotics in August, and 36Kr says Winverse has not disclosed any product or technical route.
notes: Read at 36Kr (QbitAI), which relays the Bloomberg report and names its link; the Bloomberg page itself was not read, so the url is the link 36Kr gives. Bloomberg's report is dated 12 Oct 2026, before the window, so freshness names that date and the score is lowered by 1. 36Kr English versions have shown wrong yuan figures in this run (Astribot), so figures are attributed.
